title: Agent Memory Is a Surface for Endogenous Authorization Laundering
abstract: arXiv:2609.01836v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long-running LLM agents rely on persistent memory to carry state across interactions, including permissions, restrictions, and revocations. When memory misrepresents this evolving authorization state, the agent's own records can grant authority that the underlying history never permitted, resulting in misaligned behavior without any external attacks.   We term this failure endogenous authorization laundering, where spurious permissions written into memory lead to unauthorized actions as their provenance is washed away. We then introduce EAL-Bench, which measures how accurately persistent memory preserves evolving authorization state and whether errors propagate to downstream unauthorized actions.   We evaluate five LLMs as memory writers and two as executors across procurement, cybersecurity, and finance. translated_title: 智能体记忆是内源性授权洗白的载体
translated_abstract: 长期运行的LLM智能体依赖持久化记忆在多次交互之间传递状态，包括权限、限制和撤销信息。当记忆错误地表达这种不断演变的授权状态时，智能体自身的记录可能会赋予底层历史从未允许过的权限，从而在没有任何外部攻击的情况下导致行为失准。我们将这种失效称为“内源性授权洗白”：写入记忆中的虚假权限在溯源信息被“洗掉”后，会导致未经授权的行为。随后我们提出EAL-Bench基准，用于衡量持久化记忆保存演变授权状态的准确程度，以及这些错误是否会传播为下游的未授权行为。我们在采购、网络安全和金融三个领域，评估了五个LLM作为记忆写入者、两个LLM作为执行者的表现。我们发现，在增量记忆更新的过程中，写入者会为高达50.2%的未授权请求制造虚假授权；一旦虚假……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出“内源性授权洗白”这一新失效模式并构建EAL-Bench基准，发现LLM智能体的持久化记忆在增量更新时会为高达50.2%的未授权请求凭空写入虚假权限，使未授权行为在无需任何外部攻击的情况下发生。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces "endogenous authorization laundering" and the EAL-Bench benchmark, showing that persistent agent memory under incremental updates fabricates false authority for up to 50.2% of unauthorized requests, enabling unauthorized actions without any external attack.
